title: Pipeline‐Quality Renewable Natural Gas From Brewery Wastewater via Integrated Biological Biogas Upgrading and Cleaning
content:
A strategy of H2-assisted biogas upgrading and cleaning is demonstrated to produce pipeline-quality renewable natural gas.


ABSTRACT

Renewable natural gas (RNG) upgraded from biogas is a promising low-carbon fuel, and proper postcleaning is a key to pipeline-grade RNG. Herein, a lab-scale hybrid H2-assisted biogas upgrading system was integrated with a downstream cleaning unit and operated for more than 400 days. Continuous H2 dosing enabled in situ CO2 conversion to CH4, predominantly through hydrogenotrophic methanation as inferred from gas composition and reaction stoichiometry, resulting in 90.5 ± 1.5 vol% CH4 with H2 injection rate of 1.26 mL min−1. An adsorption column further removed the residual CO2 and sulfur compounds, resulting in the outlet RNG containing 97.7 ± 0.5 vol% CH4 and 2.2 ± 0.5 vol% CO2. After the gas cleaning, H2S became nondetectable. It was found that the optimal operating conditions for maximizing biogas upgrading included hydraulic recirculation rate of 150 mL min−1 and HRT of 3 days. Correlation analysis across operating windows identified H2 flow rate as the strongest positive driver of CH4 concentration with a trade-off: A higher H2 flow was associated with decreases in biogas production rate, indicating mass-transfer/kinetic limits and the need for setpoint optimization. These results have demonstrated successful biogas upgrading and cleaning to reach near pipeline-grade RNG and will motivate multivariate control strategies and a data-driven basis for transmission of RNG into natural gas pipeline.
